channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Democrats Could Reshape Trump's Foreign Policy
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Economics' Chris Kennedy examines how the Democratic takeover of Congress could constrain parts of President Donald Trump's foreign policy, including through spending decisions, Ukraine aid, Russia sanctions and congressional oversight. Kennedy tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that Trump retains significant unilateral authority over tariffs and the use of military force, setting up potential clashes with Democrats as they seek to challenge his agenda. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Polish Finance Minister Faults President for S&P’s Negative View
item.description: Poland’s finance minister blamed President Karol Nawrocki’s use of veto powers to block key legislation for contributing to S&P Global Rating’s decision to lower its outlook on the country’s debt.
item.dc:creator: Wojciech Moskwa

item.title: Kyiv Faces Russian Missile Barrage, Naftogaz Facilities Damaged
item.description: Ukraine’s capital and the region surrounding Kyiv faced another Russian missile barrage overnight targeting energy facilities and bridges, with at least one civilian killed and several injured.
item.dc:creator: Olesia Safronova

item.title: Czech Premier Blasts Central Bank Rate Hike as ‘Scandalous’
item.description: Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis stepped up his public criticism of the country’s central bank following this week’s interest-rate hike, calling the board’s decision “absolutely scandalous” and saying it will hurt households and companies.
item.dc:creator: Michal Kubala

item.title: Finland Considers Ukraine-Style Tank Barriers as Russia Rearms
item.description: In Ukraine, anti-tank obstacles have slowed the attacker. Now Finland wants to see how such structures would fare in harsh northern weather.
item.dc:creator: Kirsi Heikel

item.title: New Zealand Government Holds Narrow Lead in Election Nailbiter
item.description: New Zealand’s center-right governing coalition has a path to return to power after taking a narrow lead in a closely fought election.
item.dc:creator: Ainsley Thomson and Tracy Withers

item.title: Burnham Bets That Britain Can Move Past the Old Brexit Divisions
item.description: In British politics, dividing lines have formed around Brexit for the past decade, often replacing traditional right-and-left allegiances. Now, Andy Burnham is backing himself to redraw the political map all over again.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain and Alex Wickham

item.title: Malaysian King Says No Ambiguity on Najib’s Home Detention Order
item.description: Malaysia’s king declared there was no ambiguity over his pardon for former Prime Minister Najib Razak, warning that any challenge to the decree amounts to defying his authority as the attorney general’s office calls for a delay in its implementation.
item.dc:creator: Liau Y-Sing

item.title: Hong Kong Arrests 28 in Building Bid-Rigging Probe, RTHK Says
item.description: Hong Kong authorities arrested 28 people tied to a suspected triad-linked bid-rigging syndicate targeting building maintenance and renovation contracts, Radio Television Hong Kong reported, citing Secretary for Security Chris Tang.
item.dc:creator: Aileen Chuang

item.title: US Believes Woman Close to Nvidia CEO Was a China Spy, NYT Says
item.description: US intelligence officials told the Trump administration that a woman who had become close to Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang was working for a Chinese spy agency, which recruited her to collect information on him, the New York Times reported Friday.
item.dc:creator: John Harney

item.title: Australia’s Albanese Urges Iran De-Escalation After US Midterms
item.description: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has called for a de-escalation of tensions between the US and Iran after the midterm elections, which he described as “very significant,” according to a report from the Australian Broadcasting Corp.
item.dc:creator: Richard Henderson

item.title: Wall Street Week | Blue Wave Economic Impacts, European Welfare Woes
item.description: This week, Columbia Business School professor Glenn Hubbard breaks down the economic implications of the US midterm elections. Meanwhile, rising oil prices are both a burden and a benefit in Alaska. And, we go into the field with Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin to get a closer look at American manufacturing. Plus, Europe’s postwar welfare programs are facing new challenges amid budget crunches and growing youth protests. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Touts Plan for US Air Show, Seeks to Turn Page on Midterm
item.description: President Donald Trump sought to shrug off his Republican Party’s disastrous midterm defeat during a visit to Florida, touting plans to launch a new US air show as an example of how his economic agenda is revitalizing American industry.
item.dc:creator: Kate Sullivan

item.title: Wiles Out as White House Chief of Staff, Stephen Miller Takes Role
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Joe Manchin, former US Senator and Governor for West Virginia, says Democrats can overplay their hand if they make impeaching President Donald Trump a priority after taking control of Congress. Rep. Don Beyer (D-VA) says he was thrilled that a federal judge temporarily blocked President Donald Trump's planned triumphal arch from breaking ground. Rep. Gwen Moore (D-WI) says affordability is “top of mind for all Americans” and believes health care is an obvious place for Democrats to intervene. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Coinbase’s Ryan VanGrack Says Crypto Clarity Is Advancing
item.description: Coinbase Vice Chair Ryan VanGrack says legislation has stalled since the Clarity Act vote, but the SEC and CFTC are advancing regulatory measures that are providing another route to clarity. He added that crypto is inherently bipartisan, even as regulatory proposals may face congressional scrutiny and debate. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Chip Stocks Rebound
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
A rebound in chipmakers propped up the stock market as dip buyers emerged despite economic data that reinforced speculation the Federal Reserve will boost rates in December. Technology stocks staged a sharp recovery, but whether that holds is another matter. Meantime, President Trump said he was tapping longtime aide Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff and that Susie Wiles will move to his political operation, shaking up his White House team days after a devastating midterm result. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bremmer: U.S. Retreat From Global Leadership Is a Long-Term Shift
item.description: Ian Bremmer says Tuesday’s election should be viewed against structural changes in U.S. policy that are likely to persist regardless of which party holds the White House. He cites weaker support for free-trade agreements and a greater reliance on industrial policy, subsidies and tariffs. Bremmer speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Affordability First, Open to Hegseth Impeachment: Rep. Moore
item.description: Rep. Gwen Moore (D-WI) says affordability is “top of mind for all Americans” and believes health care is an obvious place for Democrats to intervene. Rep. Moore says Democrats' agenda should not be “first and foremost” to impeach people, but says she will not push for impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and that it would be “hard not to vote yes” on Rep. Thomas Massie's privileged resolution. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Beyer: Democrats Were Not Elected to Impeach Trump
item.description: Rep. Don Beyer (D-VA) says he was thrilled that a federal judge temporarily blocked President Donald Trump's planned triumphal arch from breaking ground. Rep. Beyer says he is depending on the courts and public sentiment to stop the project and has legislation aimed at preventing it from moving forward. Rep. Beyer says Democrats were not elected to impeach President Trump, but to stop the war and bring health care back to Americans. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Taps Stephen Miller to Replace Wiles as Chief of Staff
item.description: President Donald Trump said he was tapping longtime aide Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff and that Susie Wiles is moving to his political operation, shaking up his White House team days after a devastating midterm result.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason and Courtney Subramanian
